action: Point the probe slightly towards the patient's head.

interpretation: Visualize the gallbladder as a very superficial structure.

action: Identify the gallbladder. Fan and rock the probe back and forth to center the structure and scan along its entire length.
interpretation: Visualize the gallbladder right in the middle of the screen.
Acquire a cross-sectional view of the gallbladder.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees. Direct the marker away from the patient's chin.
Point the marker towards the three o'clock position.
interpretation: Visualize a different section of the gallbladder in short axis.

action: Assess image quality. If visualization is difficult, confirm if patient has eaten in the last two hours. If necessary, wait longer before examining.
interpretation: Recognize potential gallbladder contraction due to recent food intake.

action: Prepare to perform an inspiratory hold maneuver for better visualization.
Instruct patient: 'Go ahead and inhale and hold it.'

interpretation: Observe the gallbladder coming into view as it is pushed down more into the abdominal cavity.

action: Instruct patient: 'Go ahead and breathe out.'
Check probe angle. Ensure the probe is not pointing too perpendicular to the skin.
Adjust probe angle to aim cephalad.
interpretation: Note that a perpendicular angle may miss the gallbladder, which sits higher in the abdominal cavity.

action: Drop the tail of the probe while scanning.
interpretation: Angle the beam upwards to capture the superior structure.
